Ugmuls 5.5e Automation · Detailed Summary

Feats and spells.
Connected to the action.

Weapon masteries, feat benefits, shared unarmed options, and spell helpers that work with your native rolls and chat cards.

Automations → Weapon Masteries

Weapon masteries

The actor must have the mastery unlocked in its native D&D5e configuration. The main Effect Automation switch controls the group; turning it off greys out the individual options while preserving their selections.

  • Sap Applies on a hit and recommends disadvantage on the victim’s next attack.
  • Vex Applies after damage and recommends advantage on the attacker’s next attack against that target.
  • Slow Applies a non-stacking 10-foot speed reduction after damage, lasting until the source’s next turn starts.
  • Topple A hit-only card action prompts a Constitution save through the defender’s owner or GM, with a source-tracked Prone effect on failure.
  • Graze A miss automatically creates its flat damage card using the attack ability modifier and weapon damage type. It follows damage automation and supports Undo Damage. Undo hides that card and restores the linked attack’s Damage/Graze controls.

Push, Nick, and Cleave remain manual.

Automations → Feats

Feat benefits

  • Great Weapon Fighting Qualifying attacks with a melee weapon held in two hands treat damage dice of 1 or 2 as 3. The weapon needs Two-Handed or Versatile; Versatile requires a two-handed attack. The minimum applies to attached riders and both Savage Attacker dice sets, including critical-hit corrections.
  • Great Weapon Master Eligible Heavy-weapon hits made with the Attack action on your turn offer proficiency-bonus damage, defaulting to Yes. It also works with Heavy ranged weapons. Bonus-action and reaction attacks are excluded; Hew remains manual.
  • Savage Attacker Defaults to Yes when available. Rolls weapon damage dice as two complete sets and keeps the higher total, with both sets available in the result details. A used marker enforces its limit until next turn start; canceling does not consume it. Normal/Critical corrections after Undo retain cached results.
  • Grappler Preserves damage plus Grapple once on your turn and recommends advantage against creatures grappled by that attacker. Later attempts replace damage, and Prone never keeps the damage. This feat toggle is separate from the Common unarmed-prompt setting.

Grappler · damage and control

The shared Grapple / Prone selector appears in damage Configuration for qualifying Unarmed Strikes. With the Grappler feat, one Grapple on your turn keeps the attack’s damage; later attempts replace it. Prone always replaces damage.

The screenshot shows that feat benefit alongside a Monk’s Stunning Strike. Grappler is a separate feat option, not a Monk-only benefit.

Unarmed Grapple / Prone prompts

Available to any creature using a qualifying action-based Unarmed, Empowered, or Elemental Strike hit; bonus-action and reaction attacks are excluded. Choose No, Grapple, or Prone in damage Configuration. Attempts replace damage unless the separate Grappler benefit is enabled and available.

The target uses its higher Strength/Dexterity save modifier, choosing Strength on ties. The DC uses the attacker’s Strength, or Dexterity when Martial Arts allows it. Separate save cards leave existing item Grapple/Shove activities untouched. Grappled is a Temporary effect for token HUD visibility without a timed expiry.

Stunning Strike resolves before a linked Grapple save. When Stunned applies, the following save is recorded as an automatic failure; otherwise the normal save is prompted. Effects follow the table’s application settings and support Undo.

Automations → Spells

Spell-specific helpers

  • Shield assistance An incoming hit offers Shield only when a Reaction is available. It spends an available limited/free use first, then the lowest eligible slot: 1st, 2nd, and higher as needed, including Pact slots. Hit/miss results refresh using the original dice; damage cards hide if every target now misses. Undo applied damage before changing the attack.
  • Hex and Hunter’s Mark Follow the caster’s concentration and single marked target. Yes in damage Configuration adds the labeled Necrotic/Force rider to the existing damage card. Changing the mark’s recorded target updates its association. Hunter’s Mark can apply its configured utility effect through GM automation; Hex retains its effect-selection step.
  • Conjure Minor Elementals Checks whether the single attack target is inside that caster’s concentrated spell Region. Its configured Bonus Attack Damage activity and cast level supply the damage. The elemental selector in the damage row remembers the last Acid, Cold, Fire, or Lightning choice.
  • Configured buff effects Optional utility-effect application uses the effects already configured on the activity, with native duration and concentration handling.

Eldritch Blast and Scorching Ray

A Pending Attacks window counts remaining shots by character level or cast level. Each attack uses the current single target and native attack/damage cards without another slot spend. Canceling a roll does not consume a shot; the window closes when none remain.
